result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.gomory_hu_tree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Build the Gomory-Hu tree, which encodes every pairwise minimum cut. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L51656-L51753){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.gomory_hu_tree(capacity=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Gomory-Hu tree](/assets/graphs/gomory-hu-tree.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: the weighted cut graph, whose minimum cut between A and F is the accent pair of edges B–D and C–E, capacity 3. Right: its Gomory-Hu tree, six edges weighted with pairwise cut values. On the tree path from A to F (weights 7, 3, 6, 6) the lightest edge, C–E with weight 3, is in the accent color: it gives the same cut value 3." width="100%"} A Gomory-Hu tree is a weighted tree on the same nodes with a remarkable property: the minimum cut between any two nodes of the original graph equals the smallest edge weight on the tree path between them, and removing that tree edge splits the nodes into the two sides of such a cut. It condenses all `n * (n - 1) / 2` pairwise minimum cuts into `n - 1` edges, computed with only `n - 1` maximum-flow runs (Gusfield's algorithm). A graph can have several valid Gomory-Hu trees (NetworkX may return a different one), but every one of them gives the same pairwise cut values. Use it to answer many min-cut or max-flow queries quickly, to find the most and least robustly connected pairs in a network, or to cluster nodes by cut strength (removing the lightest tree edges splits the graph along its weakest seams). Capacities are read as in `max_flow()`: from the edge attribute named by `capacity=`, else an attribute called `"capacity"`, else the edge weight on a weighted graph, else `1.0`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [capacity]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the edge attribute holding capacities (see above). If `None` (default), use the `"capacity"` attribute, the weight, or `1.0`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new undirected, weighted graph on the same nodes (IDs, labels and attributes kept) whose `n - 1` edges carry the cut values as weights. On a disconnected graph some weights are `0`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or a capacity is negative. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In two triangles joined by a bridge, pairs inside a triangle can only be separated by cutting two edges, while any pair across the bridge needs just one: ::: {#02c5ca5f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) ) tree = graph.gomory_hu_tree() tree.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True), tree.get_edge_attrs_by_id("weight") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (['B--A', 'C--A', 'D--C', 'E--D', 'F--D'], {1: 2.0, 2: 2.0, 3: 1.0, 4: 2.0, 5: 2.0}) ``` ::: ::: The minimum cut between A and F is the lightest edge on their tree path, which matches a direct computation: ::: {#d78026df .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} path = tree.shortest_path("A", "F", return_list=True) weights = [ tree.get_edge(tree.find_edge_ids(u, v)[0]).weight for u, v in zip(path, path[1:]) ] min(weights), graph.max_flow_value("A", "F") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (1.0, 1.0) ``` ::: :::
